operative_context: Subtotal, tax, and final amount handling must produce matching results when derived through different paths
exceptions: Pilot-specific currency presentation may require clarification before implementation, but must not create mismatches between operational display and customer-visible totals
conflicts_or_obsolete: Display-friendly simplifications that produce visible mismatches between stored and presented totals
Operational display simplifications that no longer align cleanly with underlying financial records
notes: R69 targets consistency of monetary representation across all layers. PRIMARY evidence (E1, E2, E4, E5) establishes that display simplifications must not create mismatches with persisted values, and that currency handling must follow strict accounting rules rather than presentation conventions. E5 (AFFECTS) reinforces that international billing must not override core pricing logic. E7 (IN_DOC gap) and E10 (REFINES context) identify rounding and currency consistency gaps. E8-E9 (AFFECTS context) reference authoritative source-of-truth concerns. E6 is supporting evidence but addresses identifier representation, not monetary consistency. Core operative rules derive from consistent PRIMARY statements across E1, E2, E4, E5. Filtered abstract or low-relevance operative statements: Monetary representation must be consistent across calculation, storage, and user-facing display layers | User-facing totals must align exactly with persisted billing amounts | Currency conversion, display format, and invoice currency must be treated as strict accounting rules, not presentation-layer conventions or temporary pilot behavior
